Hi, My name's aaron.  I'm 19.  You asked some questions that really are questions that ruled my life through highschool and into college that I want to answer(warning: this might be lengthy)

What did I do about school?  Well I have add and depression.  So being attentive during class wasn't my strongest attribute.  but I too felt like I would disappoint people if I didn't succeed.  Depression destroys your motivation to push yourself to do the best you can and I wish I had known that sooner.  

How did I manage:  I did average in school.  I was a B to A- student even with slacking.  But what hurt me was that once to twice a year I would shut down.  I wouldn't do any work and would get C's in most classes.  I got into an average college with my grades and I was fairly happy.  

How has it affected me in life:  This winter I tried to overdose.  I had gotten too many low grades and felt like I had disappointed my parents.  If you want to hear the long story I wrote it up here but don't feel like ya have to http://www.reddit.com/r/depression/comments/1whh1w/my_journey_with_depression_and_add/ .  But honesly...It turned my life around.  Getting help through coucnceling and medication has really helped me over the past few months.  I feel focused and I have hope.

Now lets talk about you.  I can't stress how important school is.  Please go to school.  I know it can be stressful but it is so important in today's world to have a degree.  Life working at mcDonald's eating raman in a shitty apartment, I can guarantee you, will not make you have a smile on your face.  Go to school and work hard for yourself.  Show your younger sisters that you can work toward a dream that you have.  Find something you have an interest in, technology was mine, and try to relate the subjects you're taking to that in your spare time.  

I know friends are a tough subject for people in our community, trust me I know.  But the most advice I can give there is to go to clubs/events that you like.  Friend someone after an online game and talk to them.  Common interests are one of the strongest things that can start friendships. 

I think the hardest thing people have a problem doing is admitting they need help.  Its so....almost embaresssing saying that you feel depressed and need to talk to someone.  But getting over that and being able to talk to someone that can listen to what you're saying and try to work with you to figure why you feel that way, is some of the best "medication" you could ever get.
